correctness.rationale: The full 20-vertex complex has 16140 nonempty faces (the independently checked full 2^20 membership domain), 87800 cover incidences and an acyclic matching of 8049 unit-incidence pairs. Exactly 1 zero-cell, 11 three-cells and 30 four-cells remain. Explicit signed integer Morse projections of all 30 critical four-cell boundaries are zero. The 3-skeleton is a wedge of 11 S3; pi3 thereof is Z^11 and all attaching classes vanish, hence the stated integral wedge homotopy. Standard Forman and Hurewicz results applied with exact orientation.

value.rationale: J(6,3) is the first self-complementary middle-slice Johnson case, with the same-size star/top maximal-clique regimes. Its intrinsic Čech nerve is a natural metric thickening of a highly symmetric graph, and the result resolves the complete integral homotopy type at the first nontrivial radius-one nerve scale. A pure nine-dimensional nerve having simultaneous S3 and S4 summands is structurally meaningful, not a routine Betti calculation; the exact attaching degrees distinguish a wedge from mere rational homology. It is a finite benchmark for questions about graph Čech persistence and Johnson-scheme symmetry without claiming those results.
